description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities . Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the grant award letter, the dates for submission of the annual reports are mentioned. In case of a three-year project, between 5-7 reports are obligatory. The first report (0) is a very short report which focuses on specific conditions and/or recommendations in the grant. There is no need to report on progress in achieving outputs and outcomes, which is done in the first annual report. As annex to the report 0, the consortium agreements between the partners should be submitted. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

actual.value:
Duhok University established in 2018 the Gender Equality Studies Centre (GEC). GEC has been defined as a governmental centre that belongs to the university. The Centre has a mandate to 'prepare socialized staff that can work in the field of gender issues, across all sectors: social, cultural, economic, education, health, politics and society. In the university's structure the centre has been placed under the Vice President Office. This project aimed to develop a gender equality plan for the centre, improve staff capacity and skills in managing gender related projects and lobby & advocacy inside and outside the university about gender issues. In this section we describe each projects activities and project achievements.
**1. Design & development of Gender equality plan**: Despite its importance the centre had so far limited activities and lacked a solid plan & strategy. This tailor made training started with several online workshops to enable participants to develop a Gender Equality Plan. The workshops were provided in different phase and focussed mainly on setting gender baseline, gender dimensions, SWOT analysis, gender indicators and job descriptions and gender milestones. This proces resulted in a profound Gender Equality Plan and assignment of a gender coordinator. In addition to this the University appointed 6 focal points from different departments to further deploy and promote gender equality within and outside the university.
**2. Train of the Training on Project Management (including acquisition):**The participants, including gender coordinator, director of the gender equality centre and focal points, received a TOT on project management. Prior the training a pre-assessment were provided to understand the needs of the participants. An important starting point of this training was on how to manage and implement gender specific projects. The training focussed among others on project cycle management including initiation, planning & implementation. An important aspect of the training was on how to monitor gender related activities within the university, and also how to attract new donors to fund activities of the Gender Equality Centre. The training was hence very practical. The participants worked on specific cases to develop real-life projects. These cases will be further developed a project proposals and submitted to donor's.
**3. Training lobby & advocacy: **To strengthen the work of the GEC, a five-day Advocacy and lobbying training was delivered to staff affiliated to the centre. The main objective of the training was to instruct and guide participants to design advocacy and lobbying initiatives in the near future, on behalf of the GEC. The participants were take through a series of presentations, exercises, examples and discussions to determine priority areas for advocacy and lobbying of gender equality issues and how to construct action plans for each initiatives.
**4. Road map to implement Gender Equality Plan: **The participants developed a gender equality plan and improved their skills and knowhow on how to manage, lobby & promote gender related activities within and outside the university. There is need for a strategy document ( a road map) on how to implement gender plan. Several strategic sessions organized to concretize gender equality plan, identify roles & responsibilities and integrate findings of this training into policy/procedure of Duhok University. These sessions resulted in a annual work plan including allocated time, resources and budget.
Overall this training program achieved all the noted results in the training proposal.
